title: U.S. House · Ohio's 5th District
area: Northwestern Ohio, including Bowling Green and Findlay

context.text: The Cook Political Report rates the 5th District R+12. Brian Shaver won a four-way Democratic primary on May 5, 2026 with 28.7% of the vote.

candidates.name: Bob Latta
candidates.ballotNote: Incumbent, unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary

positions.summary: In a January 2026 press release he said protecting unborn children means advancing legislation to defend them, and the release lists his bills to restrict abortion drugs.
positions.quote: Protecting unborn children means standing strong for life and advancing commonsense legislation to help defend those who cannot defend themselves—the unborn

record.text: Chairs the Energy Subcommittee of the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, and also serves on its Communications and Technology and Environment subcommittees, in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Brian Shaver
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary with 28.7% in a four-way race

priorities.text: Campaign website says the wealthiest Americans 'should pay the same tax rate as everyone else, without loopholes that let income be hidden,' citing rising costs of housing, food, and medication.
Campaign website criticizes 'sweeping tariffs and abrupt cuts to foreign aid' for hurting farmers who rely on global markets, and calls for congressional checks on executive tariff and trade actions.
Campaign website says healthcare is 'a fundamental right' and calls for an overhaul of a system he says prioritizes corporate profit over patients.

positions.summary: Says the wealthiest Americans should pay the same tax rate as everyone else, closing loopholes that let income be hidden.
positions.quote: I think the wealthiest Americans should pay the same tax rate as everyone else, without loopholes that let income be hidden.

positions.summary: Criticizes broad tariffs, saying they have hurt farmers and driven up costs.
positions.quote: Reckless policies, like sweeping tariffs and abrupt cuts to foreign aid, have shaken the financial stability of growers who rely on global markets.

positions.summary: Says healthcare is a fundamental right and calls for a systemic overhaul to reduce costs.
positions.quote: I see healthcare as a fundamental right, and no one should have to choose between treatment and paying their bills.

positions.summary: Says healthcare decisions should be made between a patient and physician and that he has 'no desire to tell a woman what to do with her body.'
positions.quote: I have no desire to tell a woman what to do with her body, nor do I believe it is my or the government's place to police access to gender-affirming care.

positions.summary: Says he supports the Second Amendment and respects gun ownership, but favors background checks, safe-storage expectations, and 'reasonable limits.'
positions.quote: We can protect constitutional rights while still putting common-sense safeguards in place to keep guns out of the wrong hands.

positions.summary: Criticizes 'mass detentions, deportations without hearings, or militarized actions against people based on appearance' as violating constitutional due-process principles.
positions.quote: Practices like mass detentions, deportations without hearings, or militarized actions against people based on appearance violate those principles.

candidates.name: Michael Veloff
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Libertarian primary as a write-in candidate

priorities.text: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, lists his policy interests as cryptocurrency and the Single Payer Action Network for Ohio, and lists campaign messages including providing guns and training to women who have experienced violence, and lowering the drinking age.

candidates.researchNotes: Veloff's Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey answers were largely informal and did not include developed positions on most fixed issue-list topics. No campaign website, news interview or forum coverage found. His survey lists the Single Payer Action Network for Ohio as an area of interest; this was not recorded as a stated position on public health coverage.

statements.quote: Guns and training for women who have experienced violence
statements.context: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, March 12, 2026, as one of three key campaign messages

researchNotes: Federal key votes and FEC totals for Latta are added separately by script. An independent candidate, Dalton Franklin, withdrew and did not appear on the ballot.
